questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

He ______ the truth.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the past tense of the verb is required to indicate that the action has already been completed.
 
• The options provided are:
 
 
• 1) **speak (present tense)**
 
• 2) **spoken (past participle)**
 
• 3) **speaking (present participle)**
 
• 4)** spoke (simple past)**
 
 
 
• **Since the sentence requires the past tense, the correct option is 'spoke'.**
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 4)

​Therefore the correct statement is: *He **spoke** the truth*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In English grammar, the simple past tense is used to describe actions that have already been completed at the time of speaking.
 
• Examples of the simple past tense:
 
 
• **She walked** to the park.
 
• **They played** soccer.
 
• **We visited** the museum.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment in which the article has been used INCORRECTLY.

Ms. Rose is a / sweetest of / all the girls / in the class.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the second part of the given sentence, the article 'a' is incorrect.
 
• The correct usage should be **'the'** before the superlative adjective **'sweetest'**.
 
• Therefore, the corrected part should be 'the sweetest of'.

Hence, the correct statement should be: *Ms. Rose is **the sweetest of** all the girls in the class*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Articles **'a'**, **'an'**, and **'the'** are used before nouns or adjectives to specify or generalize them.
 
• Use **'the'** before superlative adjectives (e.g., *the tallest*, *the sweetest*).
 
• Use **'a'** or **'an'** before singular, countable nouns when referring to them in a general sense (e.g., *a book*, *an apple*).

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The shop / usually opened / ten minutes / late.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2)**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the use of **"opened" instead of "opens".**
 
• The sentence attempts to describe a **habitual action.**
 
• For habitual actions, the simple present tense **"opens"** should be used.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **Option 2** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct statement is ***"The shop usually opens ten minutes late."***

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "late." **– This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Option 3: "ten minutes" **– This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Option 4: "The shop" **– This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

I am going / to buy a red car / with a leather seats / and a sunroof.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the** third** part of the given sentence, the article 'a' is incorrectly used before the plural noun **'seats'.**
 
• In English grammar, the article** 'a'** is used before** singular countable nouns, whereas 'seats' is a plural noun.**
 
• The correct phrase should be** 'with leather seats'__ without the article 'a'.**

Hence, the correct statement is:** *I am going to buy a red car with leather seats and a sunroof*.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• When using articles before nouns, ensure that the article agrees in number with the noun it modifies.
 
 
• **Example:** *A book (singular) but books (plural) without 'a'*.
 
 
 
• Articles 'a' and 'an' are used with singular countable nouns, whereas 'the' can be used with both singular and plural nouns.
 
 
• Example: *The book (singular) and the books (plural) are on the table*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Example:** Incorrect: The alarm has woke me up.
